Record date: 2129-04-24
South Elizabeth Seychelles Hospital INTERNAL MEDICINE DEPARTMENT Location: 4923 Olivia Parkway Suite 217, Lake Jennabury
PATIENT: Lysander Fairfax Phone: 28451903 email:bradleymorgan@example.org DATE OF BIRTH: 1947-05-12 AGE: 80 years
FOLLOW-UP DATE: 04/24/29 FOLLOWED BY: Dr. Emily Carter
CHIEF COMPLAINT
Persistent shortness of breath, worsening edema, and increased anxiety.
HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Mr. Lysander Fairfax returns for follow-up two weeks after his last visit. He reports that despite the recent increase in furosemide dosage to 80 mg twice daily, he continues to experience significant bilateral lower extremity edema, which has not improved. He states that his shoes remain tight, and he has gained an additional 2 pounds since the last visit, totaling a 7-pound weight gain over the past month.
His shortness of breath persists, particularly when attempting to engage in daily activities such as dressing or walking to the bathroom. He describes frequent episodes of wheezing and indicates that he has been using his nebulizer six times a day, along with his albuterol inhaler, which he now uses approximately ten times daily. He expresses frustration and concern regarding his respiratory status, stating that he feels increasingly fatigued and limited in his mobility.
Mr. Fairfax's anxiety levels remain elevated, compounded by his ongoing physical health challenges. He reports continued difficulty sleeping, averaging only 3-4 hours of sleep per night. He has been practicing relaxation techniques but feels they are inadequate to manage his anxiety effectively.
REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
General - + weight gain, + fatigue, no fevers or chills. Pulmonary - + shortness of breath at rest, + nocturnal wheezing, + productive cough with yellowish sputum, - hemoptysis. Cardiac - no chest pain or palpitations, + orthopnea. Gastrointestinal - no nausea, vomiting, or diarrhea. Musculoskeletal - + joint pain, + persistent bilateral lower extremity edema. Neurological - + increased anxiety, + insomnia, no dizziness or headaches.
PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
1. Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) 2. Hypertension 3. Osteoarthritis 4. Persistent fatigue 5. Anxiety and depression (ongoing management)
PAST SURGICAL HISTORY
1. Right knee arthroscopy in 2018.
FAMILY HISTORY
Father - history of lung cancer. Mother - history of hypertension.
SOCIAL HISTORY
Lives alone in , . Former carpenter, now retired. Quit smoking 15 years ago. Occasional alcohol use. No illicit drug use.
ALLERGIES
No known drug allergies.
MEDICATIONS ON FOLLOW-UP
1. Albuterol inhaler as needed, currently using ten times daily. 2. Lisinopril 20 mg daily. 3. Fluticasone/salmeterol 500/50 MDI, 2 puffs twice daily. 4. Tiotropium 18 mcg inhaler, 2 puffs daily. 5. Acetaminophen 500 mg as needed for pain. 6. Furosemide 80 mg twice daily (increased from 200 mg daily). 7. Sertraline 200 mg daily. 8. Prednisone 40 mg daily for COPD exacerbation (completed course).
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Vital Signs: T 98.6F, HR 82, BP 140/88, RR 28, O2 sat 74% on room air.
General: Elderly male in moderate respiratory distress, appears fatigued and anxious. HEENT: No nasal congestion, oropharynx clear. Pulmonary: Diminished breath sounds bilaterally, marked wheezing noted on expiration, some rhonchi present. Cardiac: Regular rate and rhythm, no murmurs. Extremities: 3+ pitting edema in bilateral lower extremities, no erythema or warmth.
LABORATORY DATA
1. CBC: WBC 9.7, Hgb 9.8, Hct 28.8, Plt 210. 2. BMP: Na 130, K 4.4, Cl 94, CO2 20, BUN 65, Cr 3.8, Glucose 90. 3. BNP: 980 (further elevated). 4. Thyroid function tests: TSH 3.1 (within normal limits).
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. COPD management: Mr. Fairfax's respiratory condition continues to decline. A referral to pulmonary medicine will be expedited for further evaluation, including the consideration of possible non-invasive ventilation support due to his increased work of breathing and oxygen desaturation. 2. Hypertension and renal function: The serum creatinine has worsened, indicating potential acute kidney injury. A nephrology consultation is urgently requested to assess renal function and adjust diuretic therapy accordingly. 3. Lower extremity edema: The persistent edema remains a concern. Furosemide will be continued at 80 mg twice daily, with close monitoring of weight and renal function. Dietary sodium restrictions will be reinforced, and Mr. Fairfax will be educated on signs of fluid overload. 4. Mental health: Mr. Fairfax's anxiety and insomnia require further intervention. A psychiatry referral will be expedited for medication management, and continuation of cognitive-behavioral therapy will be encouraged.
Patient education was reinforced regarding the importance of recognizing exacerbation signs, adherence to medication, and lifestyle modifications to manage COPD and edema effectively.
